description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, renowned for its comforting warmth and rich, earthy flavors. This hearty and healthy dish is a staple in every Turkish home, often enjoyed as a starter or a light meal. Its vibrant red hue and aromatic blend of spices make it an irresistible culinary experience.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. Set aside. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.

instructions.title: Sauté the Base
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Add Tomato Paste and Lentils
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot and stir to combine with the onion mixture.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the water or broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend to Smoothness
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it is smooth and creamy. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chili Butter Topping
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, add the dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber). Cook for about 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the chili butter topping over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing into the soup.

tips: For an extra creamy texture, you can add a potato or a carrot along with the lentils and blend them all together.
The quality of your tomato paste makes a big difference. Use a rich, concentrated Turkish tomato paste for authentic flavor.
Always serve Mercimek Corbasi with a wedge of fresh lemon; the acidity brightens the flavors beautifully.
article:
Mercimek Corbasi, or Turkish Red Lentil Soup, is more than just a dish; it's a warm hug in a bowl, a staple of Turkish hospitality, and a testament to the country's rich culinary heritage. Found in homes, restaurants, and even street-side eateries across Turkey, this humble yet incredibly flavorful soup holds a special place in the hearts of many. Its vibrant color, creamy texture, and aromatic spices make it an irresistible starter or a comforting light meal on its own. If you're looking to explore the depth of Turkish soups and stews, Mercimek Corbasi is the perfect place to begin your delicious journey.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)?
Mercimek Corbasi is a traditional Turkish soup made primarily from red lentils. It’s renowned for its smooth, velvety consistency and a subtly spiced, earthy flavor profile that is both comforting and invigorating. Often characterized by its beautiful orange-red hue, derived from the lentils and a touch of tomato paste, this soup is a cornerstone of Turkish cuisine. Unlike many lentil soups that might be chunky, Mercimek Corbasi is typically pureed until completely smooth, giving it a luxurious mouthfeel. It’s a versatile dish, enjoyed year-round, but particularly cherished during colder months for its warming qualities. Its simplicity belies its depth of flavor, making it a beloved choice for families and a popular offering in eateries from casual lokantas to upscale dining establishments. The secret to a truly authentic Turkish Red Lentil Soup lies in the judicious use of spices, particularly cumin, and a bright finish of fresh lemon juice.

## Ingredients for Turkish Red Lentil Soup
Creating an authentic bowl of Turkish Red Lentil Soup requires a handful of simple, readily available ingredients. The beauty of this soup lies in how these basic components transform into something so incredibly delicious.

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Ensure they are dried and rinsed thoroughly before cooking. Their quick cooking time and ability to break down easily are what make this soup so creamy.
*   **Onion, Garlic, and Carrot:** These aromatic vegetables form the flavor base, providing sweetness and depth to the soup.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** A crucial ingredient that adds richness, a savory umami note, and contributes to the soup's characteristic reddish color.
*   **Olive Oil or Butter:** Used for sautéing the vegetables and building the initial layers of flavor.
*   **Spices:**
    *   **Cumin:** Absolutely essential. It provides the signature earthy, warm flavor of Mercimek Corbasi.
    *   **Dried Mint (Nane):** Often added to the soup itself or, more commonly, to the optional butter topping for a refreshing aroma.
    *   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber):** Adds a mild warmth and beautiful color, either in the soup or as part of the topping.
    *   **Salt and Black Pepper:** To season to perfection.
*   **Water or Broth:** Vegetable or chicken broth can be used for extra depth, though water is perfectly traditional.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Non-negotiable for serving! A squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the entire soup.
*   **Optional Topping (Nane Tereyağı):** Melted butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes, drizzled over each serving, elevates the soup to another level of indulgence and flavor.

## Step-by-Step: Making Mercimek Corbasi
Making Turkish Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward process, even for beginner cooks. Follow these steps for a delicious and authentic result:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by thoroughly rinsing 1 cup of red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any starch and ensures a cleaner-tasting soup. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté the Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add 1 finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in 2 cloves of minced garlic and 1 finely chopped carrot, cooking for another 3-5 minutes until the carrot begins to soften.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste and Spices:** Push the vegetables to one side and add 1 tablespoon of tomato paste to the clear spot in the pot. Cook the tomato paste for 1-2 minutes, stirring it constantly, until it darkens slightly and becomes fragrant. This step deepens its flavor. Then, stir the tomato paste into the vegetables. Add 1 teaspoon of ground cumin, ½ teaspoon of dried mint (optional at this stage, but common), ½ teaspoon of red pepper flakes, 1 teaspoon of salt, and ¼ teaspoon of black pepper. Cook for another minute, allowing the spices to bloom.
4.  **Combine and Simmer:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot and stir to combine with the aromatic mixture. Pour in 6 cups of water or vegetable/chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend Until Smooth:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy, with no discernible lentil pieces. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (fill only halfway, vent the lid, and cover with a towel) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.
6.  **Adjust Consistency and Seasoning:** If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Taste and adjust the seasoning, adding more salt, pepper, or cumin if needed.
7.  **Prepare the Topping (Optional but Recommended):** In a small pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over low heat. Once melted, remove from heat and stir in 1 teaspoon of dried mint and ½ teaspoon of red pepper flakes. The heat from the butter will release their aromas.

## Tips for the Best Turkish Red Lentil Soup
Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Turkish Red Lentil Soup is easier than you think with a few key tips:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils:** Don't skip this! Rinsing thoroughly removes starches that can make the soup cloudy and gummy.
*   **Cook the Tomato Paste:** Sautéing the tomato paste before adding liquids deepens its flavor and color, preventing a raw tomato taste. This is a common technique in Turkish cooking.
*   **Don't Skimp on Cumin:** Cumin is the soul of Mercimek Corbasi. It provides the characteristic earthy warmth. Adjust to your preference, but ensure it's present.
*   **Blend Until Velvety:** The hallmark of this soup is its smooth, creamy texture. Blend until absolutely no lentil chunks remain. An immersion blender makes this incredibly easy.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** Lentils absorb a lot of liquid. If your soup is too thick after blending, gradually add more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency – typically thick enough to coat a spoon, but still pourable.
*   **The Power of Lemon:** Always serve with fresh lemon wedges. A squeeze of lemon juice at the table brightens the flavors, cuts through the richness, and adds an essential zing that truly makes the soup sing.
*   **The Butter Topping is Key:** While optional, the melted butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes (nane tereyağı) adds an incredible layer of flavor, aroma, and visual appeal. It’s highly recommended for an authentic experience.

## Serving Suggestions for Mercimek Corbasi
Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways. Here are some traditional and delicious serving suggestions:

*   **With Fresh Lemon Wedges:** This is non-negotiable. Place a wedge on the side of each bowl, encouraging diners to squeeze fresh lemon juice directly into their soup.
*   **A Drizzle of Spiced Butter:** Ladle the soup into bowls, then spoon a generous drizzle of the melted mint and red pepper flake butter (nane tereyağı) over the top of each serving.
*   **Crusty Bread:** Essential for dipping and soaking up every last bit of the flavorful soup. A simple rustic bread or a slice of fresh Turkish bread (pide) works wonderfully.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley or mint can add a touch of freshness and color as a garnish.
*   **Pickles (Turşu):** In Turkey, it's common to serve soups with a side of mixed vegetable pickles, which provide a delightful tangy contrast.
*   **Extra Chili Flakes:** For those who like more heat, offer a small bowl of red pepper flakes (pul biber) on the side to sprinkle as desired.
*   **As a Starter:** Mercimek Corbasi makes an excellent first course for any Turkish meal.
*   **As a Light Meal:** Paired with some good bread and perhaps a simple salad, it’s a perfectly satisfying and nutritious light lunch or dinner.

## Variations & Dietary Adaptations
One of the beauties of Turkish Red Lentil Soup is its inherent adaptability, making it suitable for various dietary needs and culinary preferences.

*   **Vegan/Vegetarian:** This soup is naturally vegan and vegetarian-friendly! Just ensure you use vegetable broth or water instead of chicken broth, and opt for olive oil instead of butter for sautéing the vegetables and the optional topping.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Mercimek Corbasi is inherently gluten-free, making it a safe and delicious option for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivities.
*   **Spicier Version:** If you enjoy more heat, increase the amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) in the soup itself, or add a pinch of cayenne pepper during the simmering process. You can also add more to the butter topping.
*   **Add More Vegetables:** While traditionally simple, you can certainly bulk up your Turkish Red Lentil Soup with additional finely diced vegetables like bell peppers, zucchini, or even a small potato. Just be sure to cook them until very tender before blending.
*   **Herb Swaps:** While dried mint and cumin are traditional, you could experiment with other herbs. A touch of fresh dill or cilantro could offer a different aromatic profile, though it would stray from the classic taste.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A pinch of smoked paprika added with the other spices can introduce a subtle smoky depth.
*   **Richer Stock:** For a more robust flavor, especially if you're not keeping it vegan, use chicken or even beef stock instead of water. This will add a deeper umami character.

Mercimek Corbasi is a testament to the fact that simple ingredients, thoughtfully prepared, can create something truly extraordinary. Its nourishing warmth, delightful flavors, and comforting texture make it a beloved dish across Turkey and increasingly, around the world. Whether you're seeking a taste of authentic Turkish cuisine or simply a wholesome, satisfying soup, Mercimek Corbasi is an excellent choice that promises to delight your palate and warm your soul. Give this classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup a try in your kitchen, and you'll quickly understand why it’s cherished by so many.
